text: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
notes: Links inner peace with intentional thankfulness — for women carrying invisible emotional labor.

text: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
notes: For women whose gratitude has to live in ordinary routines, not only in dramatic spiritual moments.

text: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
notes: Honors gratitude without pretending everything feels easy.

text: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
notes: Welcoming language for beginning prayer with gratitude rather than pressure.

text: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
notes: For women who need help remembering God's goodness when exhaustion clouds perspective.

text: O give thanks unto the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
notes: Steady focus on God's goodness — for women who need gratitude rooted in something enduring.

text: Give thanks unto the Lord, call upon his name, make known his deeds among the people.
notes: Invites women to name God's faithfulness out loud, not only feel it privately.

text: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.
notes: Lifts women out of self-focus and into awe — relieving in seasons of pressure or overthinking.

text: Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.
notes: Life begins with God's intentional delight — speaks tenderly to women wrestling with worth.

text: O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the Lord our maker.
notes: Humble, embodied, simple — for women who long for worship that feels physically accessible.

text: O worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness: fear before him, all the earth.
notes: A vision of holiness that feels attractive rather than harsh.

text: Serve the Lord with gladness: come before his presence with singing.
notes: For women who need worship to feel joyful and open, not merely dutiful.

text: Let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord. Praise ye the Lord.
notes: Simplicity and wholeness — cuts through mental clutter.

text: Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.
notes: Strength is received, not self-manufactured — for women who feel depleted.

text: Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.
notes: Validates endurance as holy strength — even when the day feels impossibly long.

text: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
notes: Ties courage to God's presence — for women stepping into new or lonely responsibilities.

text: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
notes: Fear does not get the final word — for women under mental and emotional strain.

text: Neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
notes: Excerpted — the comfort core. Joy as nourishment rather than extra effort, for tired women.

text: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
notes: Weakness reframed without shame — for women carrying pain, limitation, or chronic strain.

text: Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.
notes: Language to survive hard places without pretending they are easy.

text: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
notes: For women facing intimidating people or uncertain outcomes — direct promise of God's nearness.

text: And the Lord, he it is that doth go before thee; he will be with thee, he will not fail thee, neither forsake thee: fear not, neither be dismayed.
notes: God goes before — for women stepping into unknown territory.

text: Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.
notes: For women who feel surrounded or outnumbered by opposition.

text: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
notes: A compact four-part commission — for women who need clear direction rather than comfort.

text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
notes: Menstrual phase — restful, receiving verse for women who need care more than productivity.

text: For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.
notes: Ovulatory phase — channels high relational energy outward toward service and love.

text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
notes: Luteal phase — tender fit for increased emotional load and sensitivity before menstruation.

text: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
notes: Luteal phase — invites honesty without self-condemnation.

text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
notes: Luteal phase — for women who feel heavier or more self-questioning. Pairs with Psalm 42:5 already in library.

text: Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master.
notes: Mary Magdalene — Jesus speaks her name personally in grief. For women who need to feel individually known and called.

text: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.
notes: Widow of Nain — Jesus sees before she asks. For women who feel their grief has gone unnoticed.

text: And so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.
notes: Esther — courage is obedience in the presence of fear, not its absence. For women facing costly decisions.

text: And blessed is she that believed: for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord.
notes: Elizabeth — for women who have waited so long that hope feels fragile. The promise still comes.

text: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
notes: Mary of Bethany — permission to choose presence with Christ over performance.

text: And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.
notes: Woman caught in adultery — Jesus refuses to let shame have the final word.

text: And I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies.
notes: Gomer — covenant love pursuing what is broken. For women who fear brokenness is final.

text: And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.
notes: Mary — surrender to a calling she did not plan. For women facing costly obedience.

text: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
notes: Woman at the well — for women thirsty for something only Christ can satisfy.
